listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Friday, November 20. Our lead story comes from Ukraine. A major Russian missile attack hit three bridges in Kyiv. Five people were killed in the wave of strikes. The attack follows Ukraine's successful targeting of the Crimean Bridge. European allies of Ukraine say they have a united position and are ready for talks with Russia. Now the other front page stories. The International Court of Justice has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. The court found that Myanmar security forces acted with genocidal intent during military operations in northern Rakhine state in 2017. In Europe, the United Kingdom and the European Union hold a rare summit today. A decade after the Brexit vote, top EU officials are meeting Prime Minister Andy Burnham. A youth mobility scheme is expected to be approved. For your own work, Claude Platform has launched Linked billing in beta. Customers can now pay for Claude usage in your app through their own Claude organization. In politics, The Lever looks at Senator Chris Van Hollen's leadership challenge against Chuck Schumer. Federal judges have delayed work on Trump's arch for a matter of days. And NPR reports Democrats won 56 percent of House votes in the midterms, to 42 percent for Republicans. In tech, a Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting is trending on GitHub. There is also an add-on that connects Blender to Claude and other models through M C P. Simon Willison writes about sandboxes for coding agents. In world news, Iran has escalated attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz. A youth mobility deal is also expected at the UK and EU summit. In sports, the Rockets are twelve and four and visit the Nuggets tonight in the NBA Cup. The 49ers meet the Vikings in Mexico City. And Amanda Nunes wants a rematch with Kayla Harrison. In Atlanta, a three million dollar streets overhaul is set to begin in Little Five Points. MARTA has installed its final upgraded faregate. And a tax incentive was approved for the Piedmont Center revamp in Buckhead. In architecture, a London project uses the Tekla A P I to reuse structural steel. AEC Magazine looks beyond BIM to engineering intelligence. And a solar parking roof in the shape of a morning glory is on A R C H Daily. In science, NASA fired an RS-25 engine for future Artemis missions. Fermi data is helping find pulsars much faster. And meerkats with GPS trackers found their way home on their own. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Three Kyiv bridges hit during major Russian missile attack
lead.note: Russia carried out a major missile attack that hit three bridges in Kyiv, BBC World reports. Five people were killed in the wave of strikes. The attack follows Ukraine's successful targeting of the Crimean Bridge, which has been in the news over recent days. Taken together, the two events show both sides going after key crossings. Bridges matter because they carry people, goods and vehicles across a city and a region, which is why they draw attention in a war. The short summary does not say how badly the three Kyiv bridges were damaged, who the victims were, or how the strikes will affect movement around the capital. Those details will need further reporting. For now, it is the most significant new development in the war today, and it comes as European leaders say they are ready for talks with Russia.
